messages:
kyle-runtime: Heads-up — tossing an ownership rework idea on the table. Short summary: pull slot/lease ownership out of the coalescer into the admission layer. Make coalescer purely a packing/shape optimiser.

kyle-runtime: Motivation: when the coalescer owns leases we get racy handoffs during preemption and TTL expiry. That causes weird long-tail latency spikes and makes correctness proofs annoying.

omar-ml: Sounds promising. If admission owns leases, can we make preemption deterministic? How do we treat hot vs bursty tenants?

kyle-runtime: Yes — admission will issue versioned "slot leases" (headroom, priority, lease_ttl). Hot tenants get long leases + reserved slots; bursty tenants get short leases and a decay/backoff policy. Preemption becomes a lease-revocation with a clear sequence number.

jen-product: From SLA/product POV we need a knob to guarantee p95/p99 for Dedicated customers. Will this map cleanly to that?

kyle-runtime: It will. With admission policies we can reserve N slots for a tenant and assign a preemption weight. The coalescer then respects the lease set and only optimises packing inside those boundaries, so jitter is reduced.

Tina-sre: Implementation question: where does lease metadata live? If it's only in-memory we have split-brain risk on control-plane flaps.

kyle-runtime: Plan: authoritative lease table in control plane (durable store) + ephemeral node-local caches subscribed to deltas. Nodes continue with last-known leases if disconnected; leases have safety TTL so they eventually expire. Conflict resolution via versioned lease numbers.

Tina-sre: Failure modes to call out: control-plane partition, slow delta propagation, or node crash during transfer. Need runbooks for lease expiry vs. forced revocation.

omar-ml: KV cache affinity is big here — if you move a slot, the KV cache needs either transfer or a warmup. Otherwise token cost and latency spike. Any plan for that?

kyle-runtime: Add a lightweight transfer/handoff protocol: admission emits a lease_transfer event (slot, seq, src, dst). Destination can pre-warm KV ranges; source keeps serving for an overlap window. For very short leases we accept a small extra 10-30ms in worst cases.

kyle-runtime: Pseudo-event example:
```
{
  type: "lease_transfer",
  slot: "s-123",
  from: "node-A",
  to: "node-B",
  seq: 42
}
```

jen-product: Will clients see errors during transfers?

kyle-runtime: Ideally no. With prefix caching + overlap window we avoid visible errors for long leases. Short leases may have transient increased latency; product tiering can opt into "strict handoff" behaviour for zero-impact.

Tina-sre: Observability needs: lease_acquire/release/transfer events, transfer_latency histogram, kv_warmup_hit_rate, preempt_count, drop_reason distribution. Tagging by tenant, model, route is required. Also expose a control-plane sync-lag metric.

omar-ml: Add an ML metric: kvcache_miss_cost (extra tokens or latency when cache misses happen) so Optimize can suggest reservation changes automatically.

ci-bot: pipeline status: batcher-ownership-proto branch passed unit tests (15/15), integration queued. :white_check_mark:

kyle-runtime: Next steps: I'll write a short RFC with sequence diagrams, consistent hashing implications, and a small synthetic simulation (1k tenants mix of hot/bursty). Want reviewers for failure cases and SRE/runbook bits.

jen-product: I'll do product impact and SLA wording.

Tina-sre: I'll draft observability and runbook. Also let's define emergency fallback: if control-plane unreachable, nodes operate with last-known leases and start throttling after safety TTL.

omar-ml: I'll review KV warmup heuristics and the simulation inputs.

kyle-runtime: Great — I'll post the RFC link tomorrow. :coffee:
